easy.def: One more time.
examples: Say it again.
I will try again.
Let us play again.

more.def: Once more, or as it was before.
examples: The pond froze again after the warm days ended.
Read the first page again so we can hear it clearly.
I hope to visit the lake again next summer.

easy.def: Touching and leaning on something.
examples: Put the ladder against the wall.
I sat against the tree.
The rain tapped against the window.

more.def: Pressing on or touching something for support or from the side.
examples: The bike was propped against the fence.
Waves crashed against the rocks all night.
He rested his back against the warm stone wall.

easy.def: Trying to beat someone.
examples: Our team plays against the blue team.
I raced against my sister.
Mom played against me at cards.

more.def: Competing with someone in a contest, or not agreeing with something.
examples: The soccer team plays against its rivals from the next town on Saturday.
Many people voted against building a loud factory near the park.
Is it against the rules to touch the ball with your hands?

easy.def: With the mouth wide open.
examples: His mouth was agape.
She stared agape.
The boy stood agape.

more.def: With your mouth wide open, as in surprise.
examples: He stood with his mouth agape at the magic trick.
The children watched, mouths agape.
She stared agape at the huge cake.

easy.def: How old you are.
examples: What is your age?
Mia's age is seven.
Her age is eight.

more.def: The number of years that someone or something has lived or existed.
examples: At the age of six, I learned to swim.
The tree's age is over two hundred years.
Children of every age enjoyed the show.

easy.def: A very long time in the past.
examples: The Ice Age was cold.
Dinosaurs lived in a far-off age.
In the Stone Age, people used rocks as tools.

more.def: A long period of history that is known for something.
examples: People made tools of stone in the Stone Age.
Mammoths lived during the Ice Age.
We are living in the age of computers.

easy.def: An office or group that does a certain job.
examples: A travel agency helped us book.
The agency found a new home for the dog.
The agency helps people.

more.def: A business or part of a government that does a certain kind of work.
examples: A travel agency booked our trip to the beach.
The weather agency warned about the storm.
The government agency protects the forests.

easy.def: A list of things to do at a meeting.
examples: The agenda is on the board.
The agenda has three items.
Read the agenda.

more.def: A list of the things that will be talked about or done at a meeting.
examples: The agenda for the club meeting is on the board.
The first item on the agenda was the picnic.
We read the agenda before class.

easy.def: A person who helps other people with a job.
examples: The travel agent booked our trip.
My aunt is a ticket agent.
An agent helped us find a house.

more.def: A person who acts for others, or whose job is to provide a service.
examples: The travel agent booked our flights and hotel.
An agent helped the family find a new house.
A ticket agent checked our bags.

easy.def: To make something worse.
examples: Scratching can aggravate a bite.
Rain will aggravate the cold.
Do not aggravate your sore knee.

more.def: To make something worse, or to annoy someone.
examples: Running on a sore ankle could aggravate the injury.
The loud noise aggravated the baby, who began to cry.
Scratching a bug bite can aggravate the itch.

easy.def: Something that bothers you.
examples: The noise was an aggravation.
I felt aggravation.
The traffic was an aggravation.

more.def: Something that annoys or bothers you, or the feeling of being annoyed.
examples: The long line was an aggravation.
He sighed in aggravation when the toy broke.
Traffic jams are a daily aggravation.

easy.def: Acting in an angry way and wanting to hurt.
examples: The dog showed aggression.
Aggression is not kind.
He used no aggression.

more.def: Angry or rough behavior toward someone, especially when it starts without a good reason.
examples: The coach talked to the player about showing aggression on the field.
The dog's aggression frightened the smaller dogs at the park.
Words are a better way to settle a problem than aggression.

easy.def: Ready to attack or fight.
examples: The dog was aggressive.
An aggressive goose chased us.
He was an aggressive player.

more.def: Acting in an angry way and ready to attack or argue.
examples: The aggressive goose chased us across the yard.
The dog was aggressive and growled at everyone.
Do not be aggressive when you play.

easy.def: Shocked and upset.
examples: She was aghast.
He stared, aghast.
The class was aghast at the mess.

more.def: Filled with shock and horror at something.
examples: She was aghast to see the huge mess in the kitchen.
He stood aghast as the cake slid off the plate.
The whole class was aghast when the paint spilled.

easy.def: Able to move fast and easily.
examples: The cat is agile.
An agile monkey jumped up the tree.
She is agile on the bars.

more.def: Able to move quickly and lightly, and to change direction with ease.
examples: The agile goat leaped from rock to rock on the steep hill.
An agile gymnast flipped across the mat.
The agile squirrel dodged the dog and raced up the tree.

easy.def: Being able to move quickly and easily.
examples: The cat's agility is great.
She has agility.
The gymnast showed agility.

more.def: The ability to move quickly and easily.
examples: The cat jumped with great agility.
The gymnast showed agility on the beam.
Agility helps a soccer player dodge others.

easy.def: To shake or stir up.
examples: The wind will agitate the water.
He agitated the bottle.
The storm agitated the sea.

more.def: To shake or stir something up, or to make a person upset.
examples: The storm agitated the waves.
She agitated the bottle to mix the juice.
The loud noise agitated the dog.

easy.def: Upset and nervous.
examples: The dog was agitated.
She felt agitated.
An agitated crowd.

more.def: Feeling upset, nervous or unable to stay calm.
examples: The dog was agitated by the loud thunder and paced around the room.
She felt agitated waiting for the test results.
An agitated crowd gathered when the show was delayed.

easy.def: A feeling of being very upset and restless.
examples: She spoke in agitation.
His agitation grew.
The crowd was in agitation.

more.def: A restless, upset feeling or a lot of shaking and movement.
examples: She paced the room in agitation.
His agitation grew as the minutes passed.
The agitation of the waves rocked the small boat.

easy.def: Shining with light.
examples: The sky was aglow.
The lamp is aglow.
Her face was aglow.

more.def: Shining with light or color; glowing.
examples: The sky was aglow at sunset.
The lanterns were aglow in the dark.
Her face was aglow with happiness.

easy.def: In the past, counting back from now.
examples: I came a week ago.
It was long ago.
She left an hour ago.

more.def: Back in the past from the present time.
examples: Dinosaurs lived millions of years ago.
My grandparents moved here fifty years ago.
The rain stopped just a few minutes ago.

easy.def: Very painful or very hard to bear.
examples: The wait was agonizing.
An agonizing choice.
The agonizing pain was bad.

more.def: Causing great pain or worry.
examples: The agonizing wait for the test results seemed to last forever.
It was an agonizing choice between two toys.
The agonizing pain made him cry.

easy.def: Very bad pain.
examples: The tooth was in agony.
He was in agony.
She felt agony.

more.def: Very strong pain or suffering.
examples: He was in agony after he hurt his ankle.
The tooth gave her great agony all night.
She waited in agony for the test results.

easy.def: To think the same thing as someone else.
examples: We both agree that pizza is yummy.
Do you agree that dogs are fun?
We agree to take turns.

more.def: To have the same opinion as someone, or to say yes to something.
examples: Everyone agreed that the park was the best place for the picnic.
The two teams agreed on the rules before the game began.
I agree with you that we should leave early.

easy.def: Pleasant and easy to get along with.
examples: She is agreeable.
An agreeable day.
He was agreeable.

more.def: Pleasant and ready to agree, or enjoyable.
examples: She is an agreeable girl who is easy to get along with.
We had an agreeable day at the park.
He was agreeable to the plan and said yes.

easy.def: When people think the same or make a promise.
examples: We came to an agreement.
They have an agreement.
We reached an agreement.

more.def: A promise or a decision that two or more people have made together.
examples: We came to an agreement about who goes first.
The two teams signed an agreement.
The agreement says we will share the cost.

easy.def: Having to do with farming.
examples: We saw agricultural land.
The agricultural fair is fun.
I saw an agricultural tool.

more.def: Having to do with farming and growing crops.
examples: The agricultural fair showed prize cows and corn.
The valley has rich agricultural land.
The farmer bought new agricultural tools.

easy.def: Growing crops and raising animals on farms.
examples: Agriculture is farming.
Corn is part of agriculture.
Farms are agriculture.

more.def: The work of farming, which includes growing crops and raising animals.
examples: Agriculture gives us our food.
Corn and wheat are important to agriculture.
Her grandfather worked in agriculture all his life.

easy.def: Stuck on the bottom of shallow water.
examples: The boat ran aground.
The ship went aground.
They ran aground.

more.def: On or onto the bottom in shallow water, so that a boat cannot move.
examples: The boat ran aground on a sandbank.
The ship went aground in the fog.
They waited for the tide to lift the boat that had run aground.
